business_process: Store device intake and check-in (core stores)
description: Counter staff at 960 core stores create the ticket in SYS-01, record the device, fault, and consent, capture the passcode in the restricted field when testing needs it, and quote the repair
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 37,000 tickets a day enter here; without tickets devices cannot be tracked, which risks mix-ups and release to the wrong person; consumer repair revenue is about $5.8 million a day
manual_workaround: Pre-numbered paper intake forms with carbon copies; device bags labeled with the paper number; back-entry into SYS-01 within 24 hours of restoration
quantified_impact_basis: About 60% of core-store consumer intake lost or deferred (paper sustains about 40%) on about $4.98 million a day, plus about $210,000 overtime and back-entry
acquired_chain_dependency: None (AC stores use SYS-13; see BP-16)
single_points_of_failure: Single STPP instance per region (warm standby in a second region)

description: Technicians diagnose at bench workstations, order or pull parts, run manufacturer calibration and parts pairing, repair, test, and update the ticket
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same-day repairs are about 55% of volume; Manufacturer A parts pairing and calibration need its online tools; customers and SL-1 clients expect promised turnaround
manual_workaround: Paper job cards; repairs that need no manufacturer tool continue; parts pulled from the printed stock list
dependent_third_parties: Manufacturers A, B, and C (portals and tools); primary parts distributor
quantified_impact_basis: Repairs needing SYS-01 parts data or manufacturer tools stop after the first shift; about 35% of daily repair revenue deferred
acquired_chain_dependency: AC bench PCs connect to manufacturer tools from flat networks
single_points_of_failure: Manufacturer A online tools for parts pairing (no alternative)

business_process: Store payment and device release (core stores)
description: Counter staff take payment on P2PE PIN pads through the POS client, verify identity or a one-time code, and release the device
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No payment means no revenue and devices pile up; releasing a device to the wrong person discloses the customer's data; PCI DSS P2PE scope depends on payments staying on the P2PE PIN pads
manual_workaround: P2PE PIN pads can store and forward a limited number of approvals offline (processor limits apply); printed release checklist with photo ID check; customers may return later
quantified_impact_basis: Core-store consumer and warranty pickups deferred (about 80% of releases) plus walk-away risk on unpaid repairs
single_points_of_failure: Primary processor carries about 98% of card volume

business_process: Website and app booking, status, and deposits
description: Customers book appointments, start mail-in repairs, pay deposits through hosted payment fields, and check status
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Bookings shift to walk-in; status questions move to the contact center; deposits can wait
manual_workaround: Walk-in service; contact center takes bookings; status by text message from SYS-01 when it is up
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; primary processor (hosted payment fields); notification provider
quantified_impact_basis: About 8,000 online bookings a day; about half lost to competitors in a 24-hour outage
single_points_of_failure: Hosted payment fields from one processor

business_process: Mail-in intake, depot repair, and return logistics
description: Depots receive about 5,800 shipped devices a day, repair them, and ship them back through couriers
process_owner: Senior Vice President, Depot and Lab Operations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Inbound shipments keep arriving; devices without tickets at a depot are a custody and data exposure risk; SL-1 clients set turnaround commitments for mail-in claims
manual_workaround: Receive and hold shipments in the secure cage with a paper log; no device opened until ticketed
dependent_third_parties: Primary national courier (81% of shipments); secondary courier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Depot East, Depot Central, Depot West staff
quantified_impact_basis: About 5,800 mail-in repairs a day at an average of about $155 deferred

business_process: Manufacturer warranty claims and parts authorization
description: Submit warranty repairs, parts returns, and reimbursement claims in the manufacturer portals; receive parts authorizations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash, not time: claims have submission windows in the program agreements; reimbursements of about $2.8 million a day are deferred, not lost, inside the window
manual_workaround: Record claims in SYS-01 and submit in bulk when the portal returns; manufacturer helpdesk for urgent authorizations
quantified_impact_basis: Deferred warranty reimbursements (about 21% of revenue); loss only if submission windows are missed
acquired_chain_dependency: AC stores are not yet authorized for Manufacturer A; their Manufacturer C claims go through a shared portal account (gap 1)
single_points_of_failure: Each manufacturer portal is the only channel for its claims

description: Receive claims from 4 protection plan administrators and 2 wireless carriers through the SL-1 claims API, assign repairs, and report status and outcome back to each client
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client contracts set API availability and turnaround commitments with service credits; claim outcome data drives clients' customer payouts, so lost updates cause errors at the client
manual_workaround: Clients queue claims on their side; status sent by secure file transfer every 4 hours during an outage
dependent_third_parties: SL-1 clients' claim systems; Cloud provider A; couriers
quantified_impact_basis: About $2.37 million SL-1 revenue a day plus about $300,000 service credits
single_points_of_failure: SL-1 claims API runs in one cloud (second region warm standby)

business_process: SL-2 depot repair, imaging, and provisioning
description: Repair, image, and provision business and school devices; asset tracking portal for clients
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client contracts promise turnaround for fleet repairs and school-year deployments; asset records must stay accurate for client audits
manual_workaround: Paper asset receiving log; email status to client contacts
dependent_systems: SYS-07; SYS-04 (asset tracking portal on Cloud B); SYS-01
dependent_people_or_facilities: Depot Central and Depot West enterprise services teams
quantified_impact_basis: About $1.32 million SL-2 revenue a day, about 60% of it depot repair and provisioning

business_process: Data sanitization and IT asset disposition (SL-2 and recycling)
description: Sanitize devices with SP 800-88 Rev. 2 methods, verify, record a per-device certificate, then resell to wholesale refurbishers or send to downstream recyclers
process_owner: Director of Sanitization and Asset Recovery
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Data integrity, not time, drives this process: sanitization records must not be lost because they are the proof given to clients and the defense against a data exposure claim; devices can wait in the secure cage
manual_workaround: Stop releasing devices; hold all lots in the secure cage; no resale or recycling shipment without a record
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (sanitization stations); SYS-04 (record store on Cloud B)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Sanitization teams at the three depots
quantified_impact_basis: About $0.5 million a day of ITAD and recycling revenue deferred; exposure cost if records are lost is not bounded
single_points_of_failure: Depot West records are kept only on local stations until a nightly sync (gap 4)

business_process: Data recovery and data transfer (national lab)
description: Image failing media, recover data, deliver it to customers through expiring download links, and delete it 30 days after delivery
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Some failing drives can be read only once; losing an image may lose the customer's data for good, so backups of in-progress cases matter more than speed
manual_workaround: Pause new cases; keep failing media powered down; extend customer due dates
dependent_people_or_facilities: Data recovery engineers at Depot East
quantified_impact_basis: About $390,000 data recovery revenue a day

business_process: Contact center, customer communications, and phone payments
description: About 31,000 calls a day for status, bookings, complaints, and payments; outbound text and email updates
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers cannot reach the company or pay by phone; complaint handling (including snooping allegations) must keep working
manual_workaround: Callback queue; status recorded message; phone payments deferred until the DTMF service or virtual terminal returns
dependent_third_parties: Telephony and DTMF masking service; notification provider
quantified_impact_basis: Phone payments (about 1,900 a day) deferred and call abandonment
single_points_of_failure: One telephony provider with one DTMF masking service

description: Replenish about 1,100 store and depot parts locations from the primary distributor and the company's parts warehouse at Depot Central
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Stores carry about 3 days of fast-moving parts; repairs stop by part type after that
manual_workaround: Manual orders by email to the distributor; transfers between nearby stores
quantified_impact_basis: Stock-outs begin on day 2; about $700,000 a day of repairs delayed from day 3
acquired_chain_dependency: AC stores order through a separate legacy supplier account

description: Pay about 12,000 employees biweekly; timekeeping at stores
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Wage payment deadlines under state law; workforce trust
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll with adjustments next cycle
acquired_chain_dependency: AC staff paid through a legacy payroll provider until 2027-01

description: Monthly close, quarterly and annual SEC filings, SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; during quarter-end close the MTD drops to 48 hours
manual_workaround: Extend close calendar outside quarter-end; manual journal entries with review
quantified_impact_basis: Low daily cost; a late SEC filing is a severe regulatory and reputation event

description: Settle batches, reconcile deposits, and handle about 9,000 chargebacks a month
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Settlement files must not be lost; chargeback response windows set by card brand rules through the acquirer
quantified_impact_basis: Late settlement interest and lost chargeback disputes
acquired_chain_dependency: AC settles through the legacy processor

business_process: Store operations at the 160 AC stores (legacy stack)
description: Intake, repair, payment, and release at AC stores on the legacy ticketing service and legacy POS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same custody and revenue drivers as BP-01 and BP-03; the legacy ticketing vendor contract states only a 24-hour RPO from nightly backups and has no tested restore, against a 1-hour BIA target
manual_workaround: Paper intake and release forms; legacy PIN pads can process standalone for a limited time
dependent_third_parties: Legacy ticketing SaaS vendor; legacy processor; legacy managed service provider
quantified_impact_basis: AC revenue of about $310 million a year, about $850,000 a day
single_points_of_failure: Legacy ticketing SaaS; legacy processor link over site VPN

description: Campaigns, satisfaction surveys, and customer analytics on the data platform
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No customer or legal impact for about a week
